steps.context: Final synthesis over T1S2 (DESeq2), T1S3 (edgeR overlap) and T2S1 (fgsea). The governing constraint is that no analysis in this plan can attribute differences to treatment.

steps.description: Assemble the final report. Open — before any gene table — with the design statement: batch B1 holds all 6 controls and batch B2 all 6 treated, so the condition effect and the batch effect are mathematically inseparable; every gene and pathway listed differs between treated-and-B2 and control-and-B1 jointly, and no attribution to treatment is supported. State the assumption under which the gene list is read as a treatment effect (no batch effect at all) and note that this assumption is untestable in these data. Then give the reproducibility and method block: methods and package versions (DESeq2, apeglm, edgeR, fgsea), the design formula, the reference level and the named contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering, the number of DE genes per method, the p-value histogram shape, the seed, the gene set collection names and versions, and sessionInfo. Include the two fit diagnostics — MA plot and dispersion plot — before the gene tables. Gene tables carry the unshrunken log2FoldChange, the apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue and padj, ranked by the shrunken value, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header. Report the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set alongside the per-method counts. Report the leading-edge genes of each significant gene set and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. Method/version/design/threshold/n_tested/n_DE block and sessionInfo present, plus the fgsea seed and both collection versions

Leading-edge genes listed per significant set with their gene-level statistics and overlaps marked
Enrichment method-dependence caveat stated
Report ends with the design remedy (balanced batches or bridging technical replicates), and proposes no computational batch correction

plan.title: Treated vs control lung RNA-seq under confounded batch
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000 x 12 raw salmon gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in column 1) with a 12 x 3 sample table (metadata.csv: sample, condition, batch), human lung, 6 treated vs 6 control. The design has one fatal structural property: processing batch is perfectly confounded with condition (B1 = all 6 controls, B2 = all 6 treated). No statistical method can separate a treatment effect from a batch effect here — the model matrix with ~batch+condition is not full rank, and ComBat-seq / removeBatchEffect / SVA would strip the condition effect along with the batch. The plan therefore does NOT attempt any batch correction and does NOT fit a batch term (Inflexa rule R-0005). It fits ~condition alone, and every result is labelled as confounded: the reported genes are 'differ between treated and control OR between batch B2 and B1', not attributable to treatment.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) coloured by both condition and batch — with the labels identical by construction, the PCA is a description of total between-group separation and explicitly cannot attribute it. T1S2 does the actual inference: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples), median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, DESeq2 Wald test on ~condition with control set as the explicit reference so a positive LFC means higher in treated, apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold change, p-value histogram inspection, and BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. T1S3 repeats the same contrast with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and reports the intersection as the high-confidence set (R-0042); at n=6 per group the two tools mostly agree, and the disagreement is informative about low-count genes. T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — the disputed ranking metric, chosen here because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate with ties — into fgsea against MSigDB human hallmark (staged at 2026.1), then Reactome as the second collection, restricted to Homo sapiens pathways. T1S4 assembles the report with MA and dispersion plots, the shrunken and unshrunken LFC with its standard error, leading-edge genes per significant set, the session record, and — first, before any gene table — the confounding statement that governs how every number in it may be read.

The honest bottom line the report must carry: this experiment cannot answer the research question as posed. It can produce a ranked, reproducible list of genes that differ between the two processing batches, one of which happens to be the treated group. Only a re-design in which each batch holds both conditions, or a technical replicate bridging the batches, would make a treatment attribution possible.

Record the leading-edge genes of each significant set with their Wald statistics, and set and record an explicit random seed for the permutations. If either collection is absent at run time, report the gap and continue with the one that is present.
steps.context: Enrichment input is the ranked list of all tested genes from the confounded treated-vs-control contrast. Ranking metric choice (disputed under R-0108): the DESeq2 Wald statistic, because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and, unlike a signed -log10 p-value, does not produce ties when p-values saturate; unlike an unshrunken fold change it does not put noisy low-count genes at the top.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run on the FULL ranked list of tested genes, not a thresholded subset
Ranking metric is the DESeq2 Wald statistic and is stated in the output
Hallmark result table and Reactome result table, each with NES, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, set size and leading-edge genes
Reactome GMT filtered to Homo sapiens before testing, with the number of retained pathways reported
Set size window 15-500 applied after intersection with the tested genes, and the window reported
Redundant significant sets collapsed, one representative per group reported, full table kept as supplement
Random seed recorded; collection name and version recorded for both collections
Results labelled as reflecting a confounded treated/batch-B2 contrast
constraints: rank_metric = DESeq2 Wald statistic ('stat'); do not rank by unshrunken log2 fold change alone and do not use a signed p-value with ties
gsea_input = full ranked list of tested genes; no pre-thresholding
min set size 15, max 500, applied after intersecting with the tested genes
Universe = the genes tested in T1S2
Hallmark first, Reactome second; the Reactome GMT is multi-species and must be filtered to human via the pathway index
BH adjustment within each collection; collapse redundant sets before reporting
Set and record a random seed for the permutations
Do not run an over-representation test on the significant gene list if fewer than ~50 genes pass padj<0.05; state the size of that list either way
caveats: Enrichment results depend on the method and the collection; a set is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a finding.
Gene length and expression level bias gene-set testing on counts; the ranked test with the tested-gene universe mitigates but does not remove this.

Because the contrast is confounded, an enriched pathway may reflect a processing/batch difference (RNA degradation, library prep date) rather than treatment biology — stress-response and metabolic hallmarks are especially prone to this.

grounding.reason: Ranked enrichment on the full tested list with fgsea, hallmark first then Reactome for human (R-0107, R-0048, R-0098). Disputed metric R-0108: the Wald statistic side is chosen because it scales effect by uncertainty and avoids p-value ties.

steps.name: Confounded-design report
steps.question: What can and cannot be concluded about treated vs control from this design, and what would be needed to answer the question properly?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Open — before any gene table — with the design statement: batch B1 holds all 6 controls and batch B2 all 6 treated, so the condition effect and the batch effect are mathematically inseparable; every gene and pathway listed differs between treated-and-B2 and control-and-B1 jointly, and no attribution to treatment is supported. State the assumption under which the gene list is read as a treatment effect (no batch effect at all) and note that this assumption is untestable in these data. Then give the reproducibility and method block: methods and package versions (DESeq2, apeglm, edgeR, fgsea), the design formula, the reference level and the named contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering, the number of DE genes per method, the p-value histogram shape, the seed, the gene set collection names and versions, and sessionInfo. Include the two fit diagnostics — MA plot and dispersion plot — before the gene tables. Gene tables carry the unshrunken log2FoldChange, the apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue and padj, ranked by the shrunken value, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header. Report the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set alongside the per-method counts. Report the leading-edge genes of each significant gene set and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. Close with the remedy: the analysis becomes interpretable only with a design in which each batch contains both conditions, or with technical bridging samples processed in both batches; state this as the recommended next step rather than proposing any computational correction.
steps.context: Final synthesis over T1S2 (DESeq2), T1S3 (edgeR overlap) and T2S1 (fgsea). The governing constraint is that no analysis in this plan can attribute differences to treatment.
acceptance_criteria: The confounding statement appears first, before any gene or pathway table, and names B1=control / B2=treated explicitly
The untestable no-batch-effect assumption is stated as the condition under which the gene list would be a treatment effect
MA plot and dispersion plot included before the gene tables, each with a one-line description of what it shows
Gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange (apeglm named), lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, ranked by the shrunken value
Method/version/design/threshold/n_tested/n_DE block and sessionInfo present, plus the fgsea seed and both collection versions
DESeq2 vs edgeR counts and intersection size reported; no union presented as the result
Leading-edge genes listed per significant set with their gene-level statistics and overlaps marked
Enrichment method-dependence caveat stated
Report ends with the design remedy (balanced batches or bridging technical replicates), and proposes no computational batch correction
constraints: Lead with the confounding limitation; do not bury it in a caveats section at the end
Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit
Report the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as high-confidence and the exclusives as secondary, never the union
Include sessionInfo, package versions, the seed, and the gene set collection versions
Do not recommend ComBat-seq, SVA, or any other batch-correction route as a fix for this design
caveats: Any downstream reader will take a ranked gene list at face value; the wording must make the confounding impossible to miss.
A large number of DE genes here is expected under confounding and is not evidence of a strong treatment effect.

grounding.reason: Report content follows R-0041/R-0085/R-0087/R-0086 (methods, effect columns, fit diagnostics, reproducibility record), R-0042 (two-method overlap), R-0051/R-0055/R-0105 (enrichment reporting); R-0005@668f mandates the confounded labelling that opens the report.
